::: {#def-npsem .theorem}
## Non-parametric structural equation model [NPSEM]

A statistical model defined relative to a directed acyclic graph $\mathcal{G}$ on $\mathbf{V}$. Each random variable $V$ is returned by a deterministic function $f_V$, called a structural equation, of its parents $\mathbf{Pa}(V)$ in $\mathcal{G}$ and an error term $U_V$:

$$
V=f_V\big(\mathbf{Pa}(V),U_V\big),\qquad V\in\mathbf{V}.
$$

The parameter is the set of structural equations together with $P_\mathbf{U}$, the joint law of the error terms $\mathbf{U}=(U_V)_{V\in\mathbf{V}}$:

$$
\theta=\big(\{f_V\}_{V\in\mathbf{V}},\,P_\mathbf{U}\big).
$$

The NPSEM itself places no restriction on $P_\mathbf{U}$; in particular, the error terms need not be independent. The models of this appendix (C.17, C.23, C.26, C.28 and C.34) restrict them only through single-world independence (C.13).

Written in a topological order of $\mathcal{G}$, each variable is a function of variables that precede it:

$$
V_j=f_{V_j}\big(\mathbf{Pa}(V_j),U_{V_j}\big),\qquad \mathbf{Pa}(V_j)\subseteq\{V_1,\dots,V_{j-1}\}.
$$
:::
